blocks.text: The branch of chemistry that deals with the interconversion of electrical and chemical energy, electrical energy into chemical energy and chemical energy into electrical energy, is called electrochemistry.

blocks.title: Oxidation and reduction
blocks.text: Oxidation is a process involving the loss of one or more electrons; reduction is a process involving the gain of one or more electrons.

Fe2+ giving Fe3+ + e- and Zn giving Zn2+ + 2e- are oxidations: Fe2+ and Zn have lost electrons. Cl2 + 2e- giving 2Cl- and Cu2+ + 2e- giving Cu are reductions: Cl and Cu2+ have gained electrons. Oxidation and reduction always take place together, and the reactions in which this happens are called redox reactions. Photosynthesis, which provides food for the entire planet, and respiration, which keeps you alive, are both redox reactions. There are two ways of finding out whether a substance has been oxidised or reduced during a reaction: electron transfer, and changes in oxidation number.
Define oxidation and reduction in terms of electron transfer, with examples.
